name: Nandini Sahu

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Nandini Sahu is a poet, fiction writer and scholar of folklore and English literature. Her academic work at Indira Gandhi National Open University has included teaching English and directing its School of Foreign Languages. Her books range from poetry and literary criticism to folk studies and short fiction, including Sita, Zero Point and Shedding the Metaphors.

In the poems gathered here, intimate experience meets myth and a searching view of the self. ‘Manthan’ draws on the churning of the ocean to imagine love through both nectar and poison. ‘My Sense of the World’ holds an ideal of everyday kindness beside uncertainty and hurt, while ‘My Tranquil City, Tonight’ places a troubled address to a beloved against the apparent calm of the city.
